sentences.text: The name Goyocephale translates to decorated head, blending a Mongolian word for decoration with the Greek term for head.
The specific epithet lattimorei commemorates the explorer Owen Lattimore.
Small bony bumps along the back edge of the skull roof suggest the animal possessed small horns during its life.
Its teeth varied in shape, including large premaxilla caniniforms, a gap between the upper jaw bones, and regular sub-triangular maxilla teeth.
The humerus bone is strongly bowed, showing nearly equal expansion at both the top and bottom ends.
The genus was first described in 1982 by Altangerel Perle, Teresa Maryańska, and Halszka Osmólska.
Goyocephale belongs to the parent group Pachycephalosauria.
It is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
Originally, it was placed in the family Homalocephalidae alongside the genus Homalocephale.
Recent phylogenetic analyses often treat Homalocephalidae as a paraphyletic group, placing Goyocephale as a branch sister to Pachycephalosauridae or as a primitive member within Pachycephalosauridae.
One phylogenetic analysis supports a monophyletic Homalocephalidae, identifying Goyocephale, Homalocephale, and Wannanosaurus as the most derived pachycephalosaurians.
Goyocephale lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous approximately 76 million years ago.
The animal lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that the derived position of Asian pachycephalosaurians like Goyocephale supports a hypothesis that the group evolved in North America before migrating to Asia.
